T: Wouldst thou like to eat deliciously?
D: A Puritan family in 1630s New England falls apart after their baby vanishes at the edge of the woods.
P: Serve the mains when Black Phillip shows up in the yard.
S: the corn crop William can't save
Cornmeal, flour, baking powder, buttermilk, egg and melted butter mixed briefly, poured into a smoking hot buttered cast iron pan and baked at 220C for 20 minutes. Honey butter alongside.
Caleb's red apple, the one from the woods
Crisp red apples sliced thin and tossed in lemon, fanned out with sharp aged cheddar, walnuts toasted at 170C for 8 minutes and a drizzle of honey.
the hens in the yard on the edge of the woods

Eggs baked in buttered ramekins over cream, wilted spinach and smoky bacon, with thyme and cracked pepper, and buttered sourdough soldiers to dip. Fry 100g diced bacon until crisp. Wilt 150g spinach in the pan and squeeze dry. Butter 4 ramekins and divide the bacon and spinach between them. Add 1 tbsp cream to each, crack in an egg, season and add a pinch of thyme. Stand in a roasting tin with hot water halfway up and bake at 180C for 12 to 14 minutes until the whites set. Serve with 4 slices buttered sourdough toast cut into soldiers.
M: the goat in the yard, or lamb if goat's a step too far
Goat or lamb shoulder in big pieces browned hard, onion, carrot and garlic softened, stock, thyme and bay, braised covered at 160C for 3 hours until it falls apart. Barley bread.
Colonial ham hock and barley pottage
what a farm family lives on through a New England winter

A thick farmhouse pottage of pearl barley, split peas, leek and root vegetables simmered in smoky ham hock stock, with the meat pulled back through. Rinse 150g pearl barley and 150g green split peas. Simmer 1 smoked ham hock in 2.5L water with bay leaves for 90 minutes. Lift out the hock, add the barley and peas and simmer 40 minutes. Add 2 sliced leeks, 1 diced turnip, 2 diced parsnips and 2 carrots and simmer 25 minutes more. Shred the ham back in, season with pepper and parsley, and serve with crusty bread and butter.
W: from the orchard, honey and spice
Apples cored, filled with butter, brown sugar, cinnamon and chopped dates, a splash of cider in the dish, baked at 180C for 40 minutes, basted twice. Pouring cream.
K: Cloudy apple juice simmered gently with cinnamon sticks, cloves, star anise and strips of orange peel for 15 minutes, strained and ladled into mugs.

s.note: the corn crop William can't save
s.how: Heat a buttered cast iron pan in a 220C oven. Mix 150g cornmeal, 100g flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 250ml buttermilk, 1 egg and 60g melted butter briefly. Pour into the hot pan and bake 20 minutes. Serve with 60g butter beaten with 2 tbsp honey.

s.note: Caleb's red apple, the one from the woods
s.how: Slice 2 red apples thin and toss in lemon juice. Fan out on a board with 200g sharp aged cheddar cut into slices. Toast 80g walnuts at 170C for 8 minutes and scatter over, then drizzle with honey.

m.note: the goat in the yard, or lamb if goat's a step too far
m.how: Brown 1.5kg goat or lamb shoulder in big pieces. Soften 2 onions, 3 carrots and 4 garlic cloves, add 750ml stock, thyme and 2 bay leaves. Cover and braise at 160C for 3 hours until it falls apart. Serve with crusty bread.

w.note: from the orchard, honey and spice
w.how: Core 4 apples and fill each with a mix of 40g butter, 60g brown sugar, 1 tsp cinnamon and 60g chopped dates. Add a splash of water to the dish and bake at 180C for 40 minutes, basting twice. Serve with pouring cream.

d.how: Simmer 1.5L cloudy apple juice with 2 cinnamon sticks, 6 cloves, 2 star anise and strips of orange peel for 15 minutes. Strain and ladle into four mugs. Drink it by the fire with the door shut.
